##### ELA.3.3.2 — Preparing Questions

- `ELA.3.3.2.1` Think of a question to ask a friend.
- `ELA.3.3.2.2` Ask 'What is your favorite...?'
- `ELA.3.3.2.3` Listen to the answer.
- `ELA.3.3.2.4` Take turns asking and answering.
- `ELA.3.3.2.5` Write down three questions before an interview.
- `ELA.3.3.2.6` Distinguish between 'Yes/No' questions and 'Tell me about' questions.
- `ELA.3.3.2.7` Explain why preparation helps you learn more.
- `ELA.3.3.2.8` Ask a follow-up question ('Why?').
- `ELA.3.3.2.9` Analyze the difference between Open-Ended and Closed-Ended questions.
- `ELA.3.3.2.10` Interpret the silence (waiting for the person to say more).
- `ELA.3.3.2.11` Connect the questions to the goal of the article.
- `ELA.3.3.2.12` Explain the strategy of ordering questions (easy to hard).
- `ELA.3.3.2.13` Construct a cohesive interview protocol for a subject matter expert.
- `ELA.3.3.2.14` Evaluate the effectiveness of probing questions.
- `ELA.3.3.2.15` Defend the ethical boundaries of questioning (privacy vs. public interest).
- `ELA.3.3.2.16` Synthesize background research into intelligent inquiry.

##### ELA.3.3.3 — Quoting Sources Accurately

- `ELA.3.3.3.1` Use speech bubbles for words spoken.
- `ELA.3.3.3.2` Say 'He said...' or 'She said...'.
- `ELA.3.3.3.3` Tell the truth about what someone said.
- `ELA.3.3.3.4` Don't change their words.
- `ELA.3.3.3.5` Use quotation marks around exact words.
- `ELA.3.3.3.6` Explain why we give credit to the speaker.
- `ELA.3.3.3.7` Compare a direct quote with a summary.
- `ELA.3.3.3.8` Attribute the quote to the correct person.
- `ELA.3.3.3.9` Analyze when to use a full quote vs. a partial quote.
- `ELA.3.3.3.10` Interpret the use of ellipses (...) and brackets [ ].
- `ELA.3.3.3.11` Connect the credibility of the article to the quality of the sources.
- `ELA.3.3.3.12` Explain the Eighth Commandment (Stealing) in relation to plagiarism/misquoting.
- `ELA.3.3.3.13` Construct a balanced article using multiple sources.
- `ELA.3.3.3.14` Evaluate the context of a quote to prevent misrepresentation.
- `ELA.3.3.3.15` Defend the reputation of the subject by quoting fairly.
- `ELA.3.3.3.16` Synthesize attribution verbs (said, claimed, argued) for precision.

#### ELA.3.4 — News Writing Fundamentals

##### ELA.3.4.1 — Leads and Headlines

- `ELA.3.4.1.1` Identify the title of a news story.
- `ELA.3.4.1.2` Create a short name for a picture.
- `ELA.3.4.1.3` Recall that a title tells us what the story is about.
- `ELA.3.4.1.4` Observe bold letters at the top of a page.
- `ELA.3.4.1.5` Write a catchy headline for a class event.
- `ELA.3.4.1.6` Explain the job of the first sentence (The Lead).
- `ELA.3.4.1.7` Compare a boring start with an interesting start.
- `ELA.3.4.1.8` Match headlines to stories.
- `ELA.3.4.1.9` Analyze different types of leads (Summary, Anecdotal, Question).
- `ELA.3.4.1.10` Interpret the tone of a headline (Sensational vs. Factual).
- `ELA.3.4.1.11` Connect the headline to the main idea of the article.
- `ELA.3.4.1.12` Explain the ethics of 'Clickbait' headlines.
- `ELA.3.4.1.13` Construct headlines that are both engaging and accurate.
- `ELA.3.4.1.14` Evaluate the impact of active verbs in headlines.
- `ELA.3.4.1.15` Defend the importance of the lead in framing the reader's perspective.
- `ELA.3.4.1.16` Synthesize the article's content into a sub-head or deck.

##### ELA.3.4.2 — Objectivity vs. Framing

- `ELA.3.4.2.1` Identify a fact (It is raining) vs. a feeling (I hate rain).
- `ELA.3.4.2.2` Name a story that is true.
- `ELA.3.4.2.3` Recall that we should tell the truth about what happened.
- `ELA.3.4.2.4` Observe that different people see different things.
- `ELA.3.4.2.5` Summarize the difference between Fact and Opinion.
- `ELA.3.4.2.6` Explain what it means to be 'fair' to both sides.
- `ELA.3.4.2.7` Compare a news report with an advertisement.
- `ELA.3.4.2.8` Identify 'loaded' words that show feelings.
- `ELA.3.4.2.9` Analyze how word choice influences the reader's opinion (Framing).
- `ELA.3.4.2.10` Interpret the concept of 'Bias' in reporting.
- `ELA.3.4.2.11` Connect the worldview of the reporter to the angle of the story.
- `ELA.3.4.2.12` Explain the goal of neutrality in journalism.
- `ELA.3.4.2.13` Construct a report on a controversial topic using neutral language.
- `ELA.3.4.2.14` Evaluate the inevitability of bias and how to mitigate it.
- `ELA.3.4.2.15` Defend the Christian commitment to truth-telling over agenda-pushing.
- `ELA.3.4.2.16` Synthesize conflicting reports to find the objective reality.

##### ELA.3.4.3 — The 5Ws + H

- `ELA.3.4.3.1` Ask 'Who is it about?'.
- `ELA.3.4.3.2` Ask 'What happened?'.
- `ELA.3.4.3.3` Ask 'Where did it happen?'.
- `ELA.3.4.3.4` Draw a picture answering these questions.
- `ELA.3.4.3.5` Write a sentence including Who, What, When, and Where.
- `ELA.3.4.3.6` Explain why 'Why' and 'How' are sometimes harder to answer.
- `ELA.3.4.3.7` Check a story to see if any Ws are missing.
- `ELA.3.4.3.8` Interview a friend using the 5 Ws.
- `ELA.3.4.3.9` Analyze a lead paragraph to locate all 5 Ws.
- `ELA.3.4.3.10` Interpret the 'Why' to understand the significance of the event.
- `ELA.3.4.3.11` Connect the accuracy of the 5 Ws to the truthfulness of the report.
- `ELA.3.4.3.12` Explain how the 'How' adds context to the event.
- `ELA.3.4.3.13` Construct a comprehensive lead that integrates all elements smoothly.
- `ELA.3.4.3.14` Evaluate a report for gaps in information.
- `ELA.3.4.3.15` Defend the necessity of factual completeness.
- `ELA.3.4.3.16` Synthesize multiple sources to answer the 'Why' comprehensively.

##### ELA.3.4.4 — The Inverted Pyramid Structure

- `ELA.3.4.4.1` Identify the most important part of a story.
- `ELA.3.4.4.2` Tell the 'big news' first.
- `ELA.3.4.4.3` Name the 'Who' and 'What' of an event.
- `ELA.3.4.4.4` Recall that news tells us what is happening now.
- `ELA.3.4.4.5` Summarize the concept of putting the most important facts at the top.
- `ELA.3.4.4.6` Explain why readers might stop reading after the first paragraph.
- `ELA.3.4.4.7` Compare a mystery story (climax at end) with a news story (climax at start).
- `ELA.3.4.4.8` Apply the Inverted Pyramid to organize a school report.
- `ELA.3.4.4.9` Analyze a newspaper article to identify the cutoff point for details.
- `ELA.3.4.4.10` Interpret the function of the 'Lead' paragraph.
- `ELA.3.4.4.11` Connect the structure to the history of the telegraph (conciseness).
- `ELA.3.4.4.12` Explain the trade-off between brevity and detail.
- `ELA.3.4.4.13` Construct a news article adhering strictly to the Inverted Pyramid.
- `ELA.3.4.4.14` Evaluate the editorial decision-making process in cutting stories.
- `ELA.3.4.4.15` Defend the utility of this structure for modern digital consumption.
- `ELA.3.4.4.16` Synthesize complex events into a prioritized narrative.

#### ELA.3.5 — Opinion, Editorial & Commentary Writing

##### ELA.3.5.1 — Editorial Voice and Responsibility

- `ELA.3.5.1.1` Sign your name to your work.
- `ELA.3.5.1.2` Say true things.
- `ELA.3.5.1.3` Don't say mean things.
- `ELA.3.5.1.4` Use a polite voice.
- `ELA.3.5.1.5` Understand that words have power.
- `ELA.3.5.1.6` Explain why newspapers have an 'Opinion' section.
- `ELA.3.5.1.7` Compare a reporter (neutral) with a columnist (opinionated).
- `ELA.3.5.1.8` Apply the Golden Rule to writing about others.
- `ELA.3.5.1.9` Analyze the influence of media on public opinion.
- `ELA.3.5.1.10` Interpret the tone of a piece (sarcastic, serious, hopeful).
- `ELA.3.5.1.11` Connect the writer's reputation to their credibility.
- `ELA.3.5.1.12` Explain the responsibility of the 'Fourth Estate' (Press).
- `ELA.3.5.1.13` Construct a unique authorial voice.
- `ELA.3.5.1.14` Evaluate the ethical implications of advocating for a policy.
- `ELA.3.5.1.15` Defend the freedom of the press and speech.
- `ELA.3.5.1.16` Synthesize personal conviction with public good.

##### ELA.3.5.2 — Writing Clearly About Controversial Issues

- `ELA.3.5.2.1` State what you like or don't like.
- `ELA.3.5.2.2` Give a reason using 'because'.
- `ELA.3.5.2.3` Listen to a friend who thinks differently.
- `ELA.3.5.2.4` Be kind when disagreeing.
- `ELA.3.5.2.5` Identify a problem in the school or town.
- `ELA.3.5.2.6` Suggest a solution to the problem.
- `ELA.3.5.2.7` Explain why your solution is good.
- `ELA.3.5.2.8` Respect that others might have different ideas.
- `ELA.3.5.2.9` Analyze the structure of an Op-Ed (Opinion-Editorial).
- `ELA.3.5.2.10` Interpret the opposing viewpoint fairly.
- `ELA.3.5.2.11` Connect the issue to a moral principle.
- `ELA.3.5.2.12` Explain the difference between an attack and an argument.
- `ELA.3.5.2.13` Construct a persuasive editorial on a current event.
- `ELA.3.5.2.14` Evaluate the logical strength of your own position.
- `ELA.3.5.2.15` Defend a position with grace and truth (Colossians 4:6).
- `ELA.3.5.2.16` Synthesize facts and values to persuade a skeptical audience.

### ELA.4 — Literary Analysis & Criticism

#### ELA.4.1 — Archetypes, Motifs & Symbols

##### ELA.4.1.1 — Common Biblical and Literary Symbols

- `ELA.4.1.1.1` Identify Light as good and Dark as bad/scary.
- `ELA.4.1.1.2` Name Water as something that washes clean.
- `ELA.4.1.1.3` Recall that a Snake usually means something bad.
- `ELA.4.1.1.4` Observe that a Lamb means gentle.
- `ELA.4.1.1.5` Summarize what a Desert represents (testing/hardship).
- `ELA.4.1.1.6` Explain the symbolism of a Garden (paradise/growth).
- `ELA.4.1.1.7` Compare the symbolism of a Lion (danger or royalty).
- `ELA.4.1.1.8` Identify seasonal symbols (Winter=Death, Spring=Life).
- `ELA.4.1.1.9` Analyze the symbolism of Blood (life, sacrifice, guilt).
- `ELA.4.1.1.10` Interpret the Mountainaintop experience (meeting God).
- `ELA.4.1.1.11` Connect literary symbols to their Biblical roots.
- `ELA.4.1.1.12` Explain the dual nature of symbols (Fire warms and burns).
- `ELA.4.1.1.13` Construct an essay on the color symbolism in a text (e.g., The Great Gatsby or Scarlet Letter).
- `ELA.4.1.1.14` Evaluate the use of water imagery (Baptism/Chaos/Life) across texts.
- `ELA.4.1.1.15` Defend the objective meaning of certain universal symbols.
- `ELA.4.1.1.16` Synthesize the symbolic landscape of a narrative.

##### ELA.4.1.2 — Hero Archetype and Journey

- `ELA.4.1.2.1` Identify the Hero who goes on an adventure.
- `ELA.4.1.2.2` Name the Wise Helper (like Gandalf or Obi-Wan).
- `ELA.4.1.2.3` Recall that the hero has to fight a monster.
- `ELA.4.1.2.4` Observe that the hero comes home changed.
- `ELA.4.1.2.5` Summarize the 'Hero's Journey' (Leaving home, Trial, Return).
- `ELA.4.1.2.6` Explain the 'Call to Adventure'.
- `ELA.4.1.2.7` Compare the standard hero with a Biblical hero.
- `ELA.4.1.2.8` Identify common character types (The Mentor, The Trickster).
- `ELA.4.1.2.9` Analyze the Monomyth structure (Joseph Campbell) - critically.
- `ELA.4.1.2.10` Interpret the 'Belly of the Whale' moment (lowest point).
- `ELA.4.1.2.11` Connect the Hero's Journey to the Gospel story.
- `ELA.4.1.2.12` Explain the Tragic Hero vs. the Epic Hero.
- `ELA.4.1.2.13` Construct a comparative analysis of the Christ-figure vs. the Secular Hero.
- `ELA.4.1.2.14` Evaluate the limitations of the Archetypal approach.
- `ELA.4.1.2.15` Defend the uniqueness of Christ amidst 'dying and rising god' myths.
- `ELA.4.1.2.16` Synthesize the universal longing for a Savior seen in archetypes.

#### ELA.4.2 — Christian Worldview Analysis of Literature

##### ELA.4.2.1 — Evaluating Stories by the Standard of Scripture

- `ELA.4.2.1.1` Identify if a character does what God likes.
- `ELA.4.2.1.2` Name the truth in a story.
- `ELA.4.2.1.3` Recall that the Bible is our measuring stick.
- `ELA.4.2.1.4` Ask 'Is this true?'
- `ELA.4.2.1.5` Summarize the message of the book.
- `ELA.4.2.1.6` Explain if the message agrees with the Bible.
- `ELA.4.2.1.7` Compare the hero's choices with the Ten Commandments.
- `ELA.4.2.1.8` Identify where the author might be wrong about God.
- `ELA.4.2.1.9` Analyze the worldview of the author (What do they believe about man/God?).
- `ELA.4.2.1.10` Interpret the definition of 'Good' and 'Evil' in the text.
- `ELA.4.2.1.11` Connect the plot's resolution to biblical justice.
- `ELA.4.2.1.12` Explain the concept of 'Common Grace' (truth found in non-Christian books).
- `ELA.4.2.1.13` Construct a worldview critique using Creation, Fall, Redemption.
- `ELA.4.2.1.14` Evaluate the underlying philosophy (e.g., Nihilism, Humanism).
- `ELA.4.2.1.15` Defend the Christian definition of the 'Good Life' against literary alternatives.
- `ELA.4.2.1.16` Synthesize appreciation for the art with discernment of the message.

##### ELA.4.2.2 — Grace, Sin, Redemption, and Hope

- `ELA.4.2.2.1` Identify when a character says sorry (Repentance).
- `ELA.4.2.2.2` Name forgiveness in the story.
- `ELA.4.2.2.3` Recall that everyone makes mistakes (Sin).
- `ELA.4.2.2.4` Observe that there is hope for a happy ending.
- `ELA.4.2.2.5` Summarize a character's journey from bad to good (Redemption).
- `ELA.4.2.2.6` Explain how sin causes problems in the story.
- `ELA.4.2.2.7` Compare a character who accepts help (Grace) with one who doesn't.
- `ELA.4.2.2.8` Identify 'Christ Figures' (someone who sacrifices for others).
- `ELA.4.2.2.9` Analyze the consequences of sin portrayed in the text.
- `ELA.4.2.2.10` Interpret moments of 'Eucatastrophe' (sudden joyous turn).
- `ELA.4.2.2.11` Connect the narrative arc to the Gospel story.
- `ELA.4.2.2.12` Explain the difference between tragedy (no hope) and comedy (hope).
- `ELA.4.2.2.13` Construct an analysis of the redemptive potential in a secular tragedy.
- `ELA.4.2.2.14` Evaluate the portrayal of human depravity (Realistic vs. Gratuitous).
- `ELA.4.2.2.15` Defend the necessity of Hope in literature.
- `ELA.4.2.2.16` Synthesize the echoes of Eden and the New Jerusalem in setting.

#### ELA.4.3 — Comparative & Critical Analysis

##### ELA.4.3.1 — Comparing Themes and Interpretations

- `ELA.4.3.1.1` Identify two stories about the same thing (e.g., friendship).
- `ELA.4.3.1.2` Name what is different about the stories.
- `ELA.4.3.1.3` Recall which story I liked better and why.
- `ELA.4.3.1.4` Observe that different people tell stories differently.
- `ELA.4.3.1.5` Summarize how two authors treat the same subject.
- `ELA.4.3.1.6` Explain why you agree or disagree with a character.
- `ELA.4.3.1.7` Compare a book with its movie adaptation.
- `ELA.4.3.1.8` Identify the main argument of the text.
- `ELA.4.3.1.9` Analyze how culture affects the telling of a story.
- `ELA.4.3.1.10` Interpret the same theme (e.g., Revenge) in two different genres.
- `ELA.4.3.1.11` Connect a modern story to an ancient myth.
- `ELA.4.3.1.12` Explain why interpretations change over time.
- `ELA.4.3.1.13` Construct a comparative essay on a theme across eras.
- `ELA.4.3.1.14` Evaluate literary criticism (Marxist, Feminist, etc.) through a Christian lens.
- `ELA.4.3.1.15` Defend a specific interpretation using textual evidence.
- `ELA.4.3.1.16` Synthesize multiple critical perspectives to reach a nuanced conclusion.

#### ELA.4.4 — Elements of Story & Narrative

##### ELA.4.4.1 — Internal vs External Conflict

- `ELA.4.4.1.1` Identify when a character is fighting a monster (Outside).
- `ELA.4.4.1.2` Name when a character is sad or scared (Inside).
- `ELA.4.4.1.3` Recall that we have fights in our hearts too.
- `ELA.4.4.1.4` Observe how the character solves the problem.
- `ELA.4.4.1.5` Summarize the main struggle: Person vs. Person, Person vs. Nature, Person vs. Self.
- `ELA.4.4.1.6` Explain how a character makes a hard choice.
- `ELA.4.4.1.7` Compare a physical fight with a fight about feelings.
- `ELA.4.4.1.8` Identify the turning point of the conflict.
- `ELA.4.4.1.9` Analyze Man vs. Society conflicts (e.g., The Giver).
- `ELA.4.4.1.10` Interpret the internal monologue as a source of conflict.
- `ELA.4.4.1.11` Connect external events to internal character change.
- `ELA.4.4.1.12` Explain how internal conflict drives external action.
- `ELA.4.4.1.13` Construct an argument regarding the primary conflict in a complex novel.
- `ELA.4.4.1.14` Evaluate the resolution of moral dilemmas within the text.
- `ELA.4.4.1.15` Defend the reality of spiritual conflict (Ephesians 6) portrayed in literature.
- `ELA.4.4.1.16` Synthesize multiple layers of conflict (e.g., political and personal).

##### ELA.4.4.2 — Narrative Voice and Perspective

- `ELA.4.4.2.1` Identify who is telling the story.
- `ELA.4.4.2.2` Name 'I' or 'Me' words if the character is talking.
- `ELA.4.4.2.3` Recall if the storyteller knows everything.
- `ELA.4.4.2.4` Observe how the story would change if someone else told it.
- `ELA.4.4.2.5` Summarize the difference between First Person and Third Person.
- `ELA.4.4.2.6` Explain what 'Omniscient' means (All-knowing).
- `ELA.4.4.2.7` Compare the perspective of the hero with the perspective of the villain.
- `ELA.4.4.2.8` Identify the Tone of the narrator (happy, scary, serious).
- `ELA.4.4.2.9` Analyze the 'Unreliable Narrator' (can we trust them?).
- `ELA.4.4.2.10` Interpret the effect of a limited perspective on suspense.
- `ELA.4.4.2.11` Connect the narrative voice to the author's style.
- `ELA.4.4.2.12` Explain the difference between Tone (Author) and Mood (Reader).
- `ELA.4.4.2.13` Construct an analysis of 'Free Indirect Discourse'.
- `ELA.4.4.2.14` Evaluate the ethical implications of the narrator's bias.
- `ELA.4.4.2.15` Defend the choice of perspective for thematic impact.
- `ELA.4.4.2.16` Synthesize the relationship between voice and world-building.

##### ELA.4.4.3 — Plot, Setting, Character, Conflict, and Theme

- `ELA.4.4.3.1` Identify the characters (people/animals) and setting (place).
- `ELA.4.4.3.2` Name the problem (conflict) in the story.
- `ELA.4.4.3.3` Retell the solution (how the problem was fixed).
- `ELA.4.4.3.4` Observe the main lesson or 'big idea' (Theme).
- `ELA.4.4.3.5` Summarize the plot using a story mountain (Rising Action, Climax, Falling Action).
- `ELA.4.4.3.6` Explain how the setting affects the characters' actions.
- `ELA.4.4.3.7` Compare internal conflict (feelings) with external conflict (actions).
- `ELA.4.4.3.8` Identify the theme of a story using evidence from the text.
- `ELA.4.4.3.9` Analyze how the author reveals character traits (Direct vs. Indirect characterization).
- `ELA.4.4.3.10` Interpret the relationship between the conflict and the theme.
- `ELA.4.4.3.11` Connect the setting to the mood or atmosphere of the narrative.
- `ELA.4.4.3.12` Explain the function of the Inciting Incident.
- `ELA.4.4.3.13` Construct an analysis of Thematic Unity (how all elements support the theme).
- `ELA.4.4.3.14` Evaluate the plausibility of the resolution (Deus ex machina vs. logical conclusion).
- `ELA.4.4.3.15` Defend the necessity of the antagonist for the protagonist's growth.
- `ELA.4.4.3.16` Synthesize the interaction of setting and psychology.

##### ELA.4.4.4 — Protagonist, Antagonist, and Supporting Characters

- `ELA.4.4.4.1` Identify the hero (good guy) and the villain (bad guy).
- `ELA.4.4.4.2` Name the friends who help the hero.
- `ELA.4.4.4.3` Recall what the bad guy wanted.
- `ELA.4.4.4.4` Observe that characters can change.
- `ELA.4.4.4.5` Summarize the goals of the Protagonist.
- `ELA.4.4.4.6` Explain why the Antagonist opposes the hero.
- `ELA.4.4.4.7` Compare a 'Dynamic' character (changes) with a 'Static' character (stays the same).
- `ELA.4.4.4.8` Identify the role of a sidekick or helper.
- `ELA.4.4.4.9` Analyze the motivation of the antagonist (humanizing the villain).
- `ELA.4.4.4.10` Interpret the role of a Foil character (contrasts with the hero).
- `ELA.4.4.4.11` Connect the protagonist's flaw to the central conflict.
- `ELA.4.4.4.12` Explain the difference between a stock character and a fully realized character.
- `ELA.4.4.4.13` Construct a psychological profile of a complex anti-hero.
- `ELA.4.4.4.14` Evaluate the function of minor characters in advancing the plot.
- `ELA.4.4.4.15` Defend the author's use of character ambiguity.
- `ELA.4.4.4.16` Synthesize the relationship between character agency and plot determinism.

##### ELA.4.4.5 — The Role of Irony, Suspense, and Pacing

- `ELA.4.4.5.1` Identify a surprise ending.
- `ELA.4.4.5.2` Name a scary or fast part of the story.
- `ELA.4.4.5.3` Recall when the character didn't know a secret that we knew.
- `ELA.4.4.5.4` Observe that some stories go fast and some go slow.
- `ELA.4.4.5.5` Summarize the three types of irony (Verbal, Situational, Dramatic - basic).
- `ELA.4.4.5.6` Explain how the author makes us feel worried (Suspense).
- `ELA.4.4.5.7` Compare a fast scene with a slow descriptive scene.
- `ELA.4.4.5.8` Identify a cliffhanger.
- `ELA.4.4.5.9` Analyze Dramatic Irony (audience knows, character doesn't).
- `ELA.4.4.5.10` Interpret the use of foreshadowing to build suspense.
- `ELA.4.4.5.11` Connect pacing (sentence length) to the action.
- `ELA.4.4.5.12` Explain Situational Irony (opposite of what is expected happens).
- `ELA.4.4.5.13` Construct an analysis of structural irony in a satire.
- `ELA.4.4.5.14` Evaluate the manipulation of time (chronology vs. pacing).
- `ELA.4.4.5.15` Defend the use of irony to critique society.
- `ELA.4.4.5.16` Synthesize the effect of pacing on the reader's emotional state.

#### ELA.4.5 — Form, Structure & Contextual Analysis

##### ELA.4.5.1 — Analysis of Form and Structure

- `ELA.4.5.1.1` Identify the parts of a story (Beginning, Middle, End).
- `ELA.4.5.1.2` Name chapters in a book.
- `ELA.4.5.1.3` Recall that poems look different than stories.
- `ELA.4.5.1.4` Observe that plays have speaking parts.
- `ELA.4.5.1.5` Summarize the organization of a text (Chronological vs. Flashback).
- `ELA.4.5.1.6` Explain how chapters or stanzas divide the text.
- `ELA.4.5.1.7` Compare a letter structure with a narrative structure.
- `ELA.4.5.1.8` Identify the Climax as the turning point.
- `ELA.4.5.1.9` Analyze the effect of a non-linear timeline (Flashbacks/Foreshadowing).
- `ELA.4.5.1.10` Interpret the use of 'In Media Res' (starting in the middle).
- `ELA.4.5.1.11` Connect the form (e.g., Sonnet) to the function.
- `ELA.4.5.1.12` Explain the 'Frame Narrative' (story within a story).
- `ELA.4.5.1.13` Construct an analysis of the structural pacing of a novel.
- `ELA.4.5.1.14` Evaluate the use of Epistolary form (letters/documents).
- `ELA.4.5.1.15` Defend the relationship between structure and meaning.
- `ELA.4.5.1.16` Synthesize the breakdown of traditional forms in Modernist literature.

##### ELA.4.5.2 — Historical & Cultural Context

- `ELA.4.5.2.1` Identify that people lived differently a long time ago.
- `ELA.4.5.2.2` Name the time when the story happens.
- `ELA.4.5.2.3` Recall that they didn't have cars or phones.
- `ELA.4.5.2.4` Observe how characters dress and speak.
- `ELA.4.5.2.5` Summarize the time period of the book.
- `ELA.4.5.2.6` Explain how history changes the story (e.g., war time).
- `ELA.4.5.2.7` Compare the culture in the book with our culture today.
- `ELA.4.5.2.8` Identify old-fashioned words or customs.
- `ELA.4.5.2.9` Analyze how the author's life influenced the book.
- `ELA.4.5.2.10` Interpret the social issues addressed in the text (e.g., poverty, slavery).
- `ELA.4.5.2.11` Connect the story to specific historical events.
- `ELA.4.5.2.12` Explain the danger of 'Presentism' (judging the past by today's standards).
- `ELA.4.5.2.13` Construct a biographical criticism of a text.
- `ELA.4.5.2.14` Evaluate the influence of the 'Zeitgeist' (Spirit of the Age) on the work.
- `ELA.4.5.2.15` Defend the text as a product of its time while finding universal truth.
- `ELA.4.5.2.16` Synthesize historical research with literary analysis.

#### ELA.4.6 — Literary Devices & Techniques (Language Analysis)

##### ELA.4.6.1 — Allusion and Intertextuality

- `ELA.4.6.1.1` Identify when a story reminds us of another story.
- `ELA.4.6.1.2` Name a Bible story mentioned in a book.
- `ELA.4.6.1.3` Recall that stories borrow from each other.
- `ELA.4.6.1.4` Observe similarities between characters.
- `ELA.4.6.1.5` Summarize what an Allusion is (a reference to another work).
- `ELA.4.6.1.6` Explain a reference to Greek Mythology or the Bible.
- `ELA.4.6.1.7` Compare a modern story to an old fairy tale.
- `ELA.4.6.1.8` Identify when a character quotes another book.
- `ELA.4.6.1.9` Analyze the effect of Biblical allusions in literature.
- `ELA.4.6.1.10` Interpret how knowing the source text adds meaning.
- `ELA.4.6.1.11` Connect a parody to the original work.
- `ELA.4.6.1.12` Explain the concept of a literary tradition.
- `ELA.4.6.1.13` Construct an analysis of Intertextuality (dialogue between texts).
- `ELA.4.6.1.14` Evaluate the dependence of Western Literature on the Bible and Shakespeare.
- `ELA.4.6.1.15` Defend the necessity of cultural literacy to understand allusions.
- `ELA.4.6.1.16` Synthesize the layers of meaning added by specific allusions.

##### ELA.4.6.2 — Figurative Language

- `ELA.4.6.2.1` Identify when words mean something different than what they say.
- `ELA.4.6.2.2` Name 'brave as a lion' (Simile).
- `ELA.4.6.2.3` Recall that animals talking is make-believe (Personification).
- `ELA.4.6.2.4` Observe 'picture words'.
- `ELA.4.6.2.5` Summarize the difference between Simile and Metaphor.
- `ELA.4.6.2.6` Explain Personification (giving human traits to objects).
- `ELA.4.6.2.7` Compare literal language with figurative language.
- `ELA.4.6.2.8` Identify Hyperbole (exaggeration).
- `ELA.4.6.2.9` Analyze the effectiveness of an Extended Metaphor.
- `ELA.4.6.2.10` Interpret the use of Idioms in dialogue.
- `ELA.4.6.2.11` Connect imagery to the five senses.
- `ELA.4.6.2.12` Explain how figurative language clarifies complex ideas.
- `ELA.4.6.2.13` Construct original metaphors to explain abstract concepts.
- `ELA.4.6.2.14` Evaluate the use of Synecdoche (part for whole) and Metonymy.
- `ELA.4.6.2.15` Defend the cognitive necessity of metaphor in human thought.
- `ELA.4.6.2.16` Synthesize a pattern of imagery to find the theme.

##### ELA.4.6.3 — Motifs, Repetition, and Leitmotifs

- `ELA.4.6.3.1` Identify things that show up again and again in a story.
- `ELA.4.6.3.2` Name a repeated phrase (like 'I'll huff and I'll puff').
- `ELA.4.6.3.3` Recall that repeating helps us remember.
- `ELA.4.6.3.4` Observe patterns in colors or objects.
- `ELA.4.6.3.5` Summarize a recurring object (like a ring or a sword).
- `ELA.4.6.3.6` Explain why the author repeats certain words.
- `ELA.4.6.3.7` Compare a Motif (recurring element) with a Theme (message).
- `ELA.4.6.3.8` Identify the 'Leitmotif' of a character (a musical theme or phrase).
- `ELA.4.6.3.9` Analyze how a motif changes meaning over the course of the book.
- `ELA.4.6.3.10` Interpret the repetition of 'light' and 'dark' imagery.
- `ELA.4.6.3.11` Connect recurring symbols to the central conflict.
- `ELA.4.6.3.12` Explain the unifying effect of motifs.
- `ELA.4.6.3.13` Construct a tracking of a specific motif through a novel.
- `ELA.4.6.3.14` Evaluate the subtlety vs. heavy-handedness of repetition.
- `ELA.4.6.3.15` Defend the use of Leitmotif for character development.
- `ELA.4.6.3.16` Synthesize multiple motifs to interpret the author's worldview.

### ELA.5 — Literature by Genre & Form

#### ELA.5.1 — Allegory & Symbolic Narrative

##### ELA.5.1.1 — Biblical Parables and Metaphor

- `ELA.5.1.1.1` Identify a story Jesus told to teach a lesson.
- `ELA.5.1.1.2` Name the Lost Sheep.
- `ELA.5.1.1.3` Recall that the seed means God's Word.
- `ELA.5.1.1.4` Observe that earthly stories have heavenly meanings.
- `ELA.5.1.1.5` Summarize the Good Samaritan.
- `ELA.5.1.1.6` Explain what a Parable is (comparison).
- `ELA.5.1.1.7` Compare the Wise Builder with the Foolish Builder.
- `ELA.5.1.1.8` Identify the "surprise" in the parable.
- `ELA.5.1.1.9` Analyze the Prodigal Son (The Waiting Father).
- `ELA.5.1.1.10` Interpret the symbolism of the Vineyard.
- `ELA.5.1.1.11` Connect parables to the Kingdom of God.
- `ELA.5.1.1.12` Explain the purpose of parables (reveal and conceal).
- `ELA.5.1.1.13` Construct a modern parable to teach a truth.
- `ELA.5.1.1.14` Evaluate the cultural context of agricultural metaphors.
- `ELA.5.1.1.15` Defend the authority of Jesus' teaching method.
- `ELA.5.1.1.16` Synthesize hermeneutics with literary appreciation.

##### ELA.5.1.2 — Classic Allegories (Pilgrim's Progress, Narnia, Faerie Queene)

- `ELA.5.1.2.1` Identify Aslan as Jesus.
- `ELA.5.1.2.2` Name Christian on his journey to the Celestial City.
- `ELA.5.1.2.3` Recall that names tell us who people are (e.g., Giant Despair).
- `ELA.5.1.2.4` Observe the Stone Table breaking.
- `ELA.5.1.2.5` Summarize the plot of "The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe".
- `ELA.5.1.2.6` Explain what an Allegory is (story with a hidden meaning).
- `ELA.5.1.2.7` Compare the City of Destruction with the World.
- `ELA.5.1.2.8` Identify the Redcrosse Knight (Holiness).
- `ELA.5.1.2.9` Analyze the theological depth of Bunyan’s work.
- `ELA.5.1.2.10` Interpret the "Deeper Magic" in Narnia.
- `ELA.5.1.2.11` Connect Animal Farm to political history (intro).
- `ELA.5.1.2.12` Explain the difference between strict allegory and "supposal" (Lewis).
- `ELA.5.1.2.13` Construct a map of an allegorical journey.
- `ELA.5.1.2.14` Evaluate the effectiveness of allegory vs. direct teaching.
- `ELA.5.1.2.15` Defend the use of imagination to grasp truth.
- `ELA.5.1.2.16` Synthesize the history of allegorical interpretation.

##### ELA.5.1.3 — Interpreting Symbols and Types

- `ELA.5.1.3.1` Identify a dove as peace.
- `ELA.5.1.3.2` Name a cross as a symbol of Jesus.
- `ELA.5.1.3.3` Recall that colors mean things (Red = stop/blood).
- `ELA.5.1.3.4` Observe symbols in church.
- `ELA.5.1.3.5` Summarize standard literary symbols (seasons, water, light).
- `ELA.5.1.3.6` Explain Typology (Joseph as a type of Christ).
- `ELA.5.1.3.7` Compare a sign (literal) with a symbol (figurative).
- `ELA.5.1.3.8` Identify the "Christ Figure" in literature.
- `ELA.5.1.3.9` Analyze the use of light and dark imagery.
- `ELA.5.1.3.10` Interpret the symbolism of the "journey".
- `ELA.5.1.3.11` Connect biblical types to New Testament fulfillment.
- `ELA.5.1.3.12` Explain archetypal symbols (water for cleansing/death).
- `ELA.5.1.3.13` Construct a symbolic analysis of a short story.
- `ELA.5.1.3.14` Evaluate the consistency of a symbol's use.
- `ELA.5.1.3.15` Defend the richness of symbolic language.
- `ELA.5.1.3.16` Synthesize semiotics with literary criticism.

##### ELA.5.1.4 — Writing Allegory and Fable

- `ELA.5.1.4.1` Tell a story about animals that act like people.
- `ELA.5.1.4.2` Give characters names like "Grumpy" or "Happy".
- `ELA.5.1.4.3` Recall that the story teaches a lesson.
- `ELA.5.1.4.4` Draw the moral at the end.
- `ELA.5.1.4.5` Summarize how to write a fable (short, animals, lesson).
- `ELA.5.1.4.6` Explain personification.
- `ELA.5.1.4.7` Create a character representing a virtue (e.g., Patience).

##### ELA.5.6.4 — Sound Devices

#### ELA.5.7 — Short Story & Novella

- `ELA.5.7.2.15` Defend the aesthetic value of unity.

- `ELA.6.5.2.11` Connect myth to the human longing for the transcendent.
- `ELA.6.5.2.12` Explain the difference between Myth and History.
- `ELA.6.5.2.13` Construct a comparative essay on Flood myths vs. Genesis.
- `ELA.6.5.2.14` Evaluate C.S. Lewis's view of Christianity as the 'Myth that became Fact'.
- `ELA.6.5.2.15` Defend the historicity of the Gospel against the 'Christ-myth' theory.
- `ELA.6.5.2.16` Synthesize the study of mythology to understand cultural anthropology.

#### ELA.6.6 — World Literature (Global Narratives)

##### ELA.6.6.1 — European Literature Beyond Britain

- `ELA.6.6.1.1` Identify fairy tales from France (Cinderella) and Germany (Hansel and Gretel).
- `ELA.6.6.1.2` Name Pinocchio (Italy) or Pippi Longstocking (Sweden).
- `ELA.6.6.1.3` Recall that stories come from many countries.
- `ELA.6.6.1.4` Observe different settings in pictures.
- `ELA.6.6.1.5` Summarize a story by Hans Christian Andersen.
- `ELA.6.6.1.6` Explain the story of Heidi or The Swiss Family Robinson.
- `ELA.6.6.1.7` Compare a French fairy tale with a German one.
- `ELA.6.6.1.8` Locate the country of origin for a story on a map.
- `ELA.6.6.1.9` Analyze the moral dilemmas in Les Misérables (adapted).
- `ELA.6.6.1.10` Interpret the short stories of Tolstoy or Chekhov.
- `ELA.6.6.1.11` Connect 'The Three Musketeers' to history.
- `ELA.6.6.1.12` Explain the concept of a 'translation'.
- `ELA.6.6.1.13` Construct an analysis of Dostoevsky's 'Crime and Punishment'.
- `ELA.6.6.1.14` Evaluate Dante's 'Divine Comedy' through a theological lens.
- `ELA.6.6.1.15` Defend the universal themes in Cervantes' 'Don Quixote'.
- `ELA.6.6.1.16` Synthesize the influence of the French Revolution on European lit.

##### ELA.6.6.2 — Non-Western Narratives

- `ELA.6.6.2.1` Identify stories about Anansi the Spider (Africa).
- `ELA.6.6.2.2` Name Mulan (China) or Aladdin (Middle East).
- `ELA.6.6.2.3` Recall that people tell stories everywhere.
- `ELA.6.6.2.4` Observe art styles from different cultures in books.
- `ELA.6.6.2.5` Summarize a Jataka Tale or a story from 1001 Nights.
- `ELA.6.6.2.6` Explain a Haiku poem.
- `ELA.6.6.2.7` Compare a Native American legend with a Bible story.
- `ELA.6.6.2.8` Read a biography of a missionary in Asia or Africa.
- `ELA.6.6.2.9` Analyze the themes in 'Things Fall Apart' (Chinua Achebe).
- `ELA.6.6.2.10` Interpret the cultural context of 'The Good Earth' or 'Cry, the Beloved Country'.
- `ELA.6.6.2.11` Connect Haiku and Tank poetry to Zen aesthetics (and contrast with Christianity).
- `ELA.6.6.2.12` Explain the oral tradition of the Griot.
- `ELA.6.6.2.13` Construct a comparative essay on Eastern vs. Western narrative structures.
- `ELA.6.6.2.14` Evaluate the worldview of Confucius or Lao Tzu in Chinese literature.
- `ELA.6.6.2.15` Defend the value of reading literature in translation to build empathy.
- `ELA.6.6.2.16` Synthesize the post-colonial themes in modern African or Indian literature.

### ELA.7 — Media Literacy & Critical Viewing

#### ELA.7.1 — Advertising, Persuasion & Propaganda

##### ELA.7.1.1 — Basic Marketing Techniques

- `ELA.7.1.1.1` Identify a commercial.
- `ELA.7.1.1.2` Name what they are trying to sell.
- `ELA.7.1.1.3` Recall that ads make toys look better than they are.
- `ELA.7.1.1.4` Observe that ads want our money.
- `ELA.7.1.1.5` Summarize who the ad is talking to (Target Audience).
- `ELA.7.1.1.6` Explain how they make you want it (fun music, cool kids).
- `ELA.7.1.1.7` Compare the promise in the ad with reality.
- `ELA.7.1.1.8` Identify a logo or slogan.
- `ELA.7.1.1.9` Analyze the 'Problem/Solution' format of advertising.
- `ELA.7.1.1.10` Interpret the lifestyle being sold, not just the product.
- `ELA.7.1.1.11` Connect consumerism to discontentment.
- `ELA.7.1.1.12` Explain 'Branding' and identity.
- `ELA.7.1.1.13` Construct a deconstruction of a sophisticated ad campaign.
- `ELA.7.1.1.14` Evaluate the ethics of data-driven targeted advertising.
- `ELA.7.1.1.15` Defend stewardship against the pressure to consume.
- `ELA.7.1.1.16` Synthesize the psychological triggers used in marketing.

##### ELA.7.1.2 — Propaganda Devices

- `ELA.7.1.2.1` Identify when someone wants us to join a group.
- `ELA.7.1.2.2` Name 'Everyone is doing it!' (Bandwagon).
- `ELA.7.1.2.3` Recall that we should think for ourselves.
- `ELA.7.1.2.4` Observe posters that tell us what to think.
- `ELA.7.1.2.5` Summarize the Bandwagon technique.
- `ELA.7.1.2.6` Explain 'Name-Calling' in persuasion.
- `ELA.7.1.2.7` Compare a fact with a persuasion trick.
- `ELA.7.1.2.8` Identify 'Glittering Generalities' (words that sound good but mean nothing).
- `ELA.7.1.2.9` Recognize 'Card Stacking' (showing only the good side).
- `ELA.7.1.2.10` Analyze wartime or political propaganda posters.
- `ELA.7.1.2.11` Interpret the use of 'Transfer' (using symbols to borrow authority).
- `ELA.7.1.2.12` Connect 'Plain Folks' appeal to political campaigns.
- `ELA.7.1.2.13` Explain the use of fear as a motivator.
- `ELA.7.1.2.14` Construct an analysis of modern propaganda (memes, viral trends).
- `ELA.7.1.2.15` Evaluate the fine line between persuasion and manipulation.
- `ELA.7.1.2.16` Defend the necessity of independent thought.
- `ELA.7.1.2.17` Synthesize the history of propaganda from WWI to the present.

#### ELA.7.2 — Bias, Framing & Agenda in Media

##### ELA.7.2.1 — Headline Framing and Story Selection

- `ELA.7.2.1.1` Identify the title of a story.
- `ELA.7.2.1.2` Name a scary headline vs. a happy one.
- `ELA.7.2.1.3` Recall that headlines try to grab us.
- `ELA.7.2.1.4` Observe that different channels show different stories.
- `ELA.7.2.1.5` Summarize the main idea of a news headline.
- `ELA.7.2.1.6` Explain why some stories are chosen and others aren't (Agenda).
- `ELA.7.2.1.7` Compare two headlines about the same event.
- `ELA.7.2.1.8` Identify 'Clickbait' (tricking you to click).
- `ELA.7.2.1.9` Analyze how the placement of a story (front page vs. back) indicates importance.
- `ELA.7.2.1.10` Interpret the use of passive voice to hide responsibility in headlines.
- `ELA.7.2.1.11` Connect story selection to the target audience.
- `ELA.7.2.1.12` Explain the concept of 'Agenda Setting'.
- `ELA.7.2.1.13` Construct a comparative analysis of news coverage from opposing outlets.
- `ELA.7.2.1.14` Evaluate the impact of sensationalism on truth.
- `ELA.7.2.1.15` Defend the necessity of reading past the headline.
- `ELA.7.2.1.16` Synthesize how framing shapes public perception of reality.

##### ELA.7.2.2 — Loaded Language and Emotional Appeals

- `ELA.7.2.2.1` Identify words that make us feel mad or sad.
- `ELA.7.2.2.2` Name 'good guy' and 'bad guy' words.
- `ELA.7.2.2.3` Recall that words have power.
- `ELA.7.2.2.4` Observe when music makes a video feel scary.
- `ELA.7.2.2.5` Summarize how adjectives change the meaning (e.g., 'mob' vs. 'crowd').
- `ELA.7.2.2.6` Explain how music or pictures manipulate feelings.
- `ELA.7.2.2.7` Compare a fact with an emotional opinion.
- `ELA.7.2.2.8` Identify words that exaggerate.
- `ELA.7.2.2.9` Analyze the use of Euphemisms (softening reality) and Dysphemisms (hardening reality).
- `ELA.7.2.2.10` Interpret the rhetorical goal of fear-mongering.
- `ELA.7.2.2.11` Connect emotional appeals to the bypassing of logic.
- `ELA.7.2.2.12` Explain 'Connotation' in media language.
- `ELA.7.2.2.13` Construct a critique of a partisan editorial.
- `ELA.7.2.2.14` Evaluate the use of 'Virtue Signaling' or 'Dog Whistles'.
- `ELA.7.2.2.15` Defend the Christian commitment to charitable speech in a polarized age.
- `ELA.7.2.2.16` Synthesize the relationship between language control and thought control (Orwellian concepts).

##### ELA.7.2.3 — Recognizing Ideological Narratives

- `ELA.7.2.3.1` Identify the 'lesson' of a movie.
- `ELA.7.2.3.2` Name what the bad guy believes.
- `ELA.7.2.3.3` Recall that not everyone thinks like us.
- `ELA.7.2.3.4` Ask 'Is that true?'
- `ELA.7.2.3.5` Summarize the worldview of a main character.
- `ELA.7.2.3.6` Explain that movies and shows teach us how to live.
- `ELA.7.2.3.7` Compare the message of a movie with the Bible.
- `ELA.7.2.3.8` Identify when a story makes fun of something good.
- `ELA.7.2.3.9` Analyze the underlying assumptions of a news report.
- `ELA.7.2.3.10` Interpret the 'Narrative' (the story being sold).
- `ELA.7.2.3.11` Connect media messages to secular humanism or materialism.
- `ELA.7.2.3.12` Explain how repetition normalizes ideas (Overton Window).
- `ELA.7.2.3.13` Construct a worldview analysis of a popular cultural artifact.
- `ELA.7.2.3.14` Evaluate the subtle injection of ideology into entertainment.
- `ELA.7.2.3.15` Defend the Christian worldview against cultural narratives.
- `ELA.7.2.3.16` Synthesize the concept of 'Cultural Hegemony' (dominant ideas).

#### ELA.7.3 — Film & Visual Storytelling as Text

##### ELA.7.3.1 — Cinematic Techniques

- `ELA.7.3.1.1` Identify happy music vs. scary music in a movie.
- `ELA.7.3.1.2` Name a 'close-up' on a face.
- `ELA.7.3.1.3` Recall that movies are made of many pictures.
- `ELA.7.3.1.4` Observe colors (bright vs. dark).
- `ELA.7.3.1.5` Summarize how music tells us how to feel.
- `ELA.7.3.1.6` Explain a camera angle (looking up makes someone look big/strong).
- `ELA.7.3.1.7` Compare a cartoon with a live-action movie.
- `ELA.7.3.1.8` Identify sound effects (Foley).
- `ELA.7.3.1.9` Analyze the use of lighting (Chiaroscuro) to create mood.
- `ELA.7.3.1.10` Interpret the composition of a frame (Rule of Thirds).
- `ELA.7.3.1.11` Connect the editing speed (cuts) to the pacing of the scene.
- `ELA.7.3.1.12` Explain the 'Kuleshov Effect' (how editing changes meaning).
- `ELA.7.3.1.13` Construct a scene analysis of a classic film.
- `ELA.7.3.1.14` Evaluate the director's use of Mise-en-scène.
- `ELA.7.3.1.15` Defend film as a serious art form comparable to literature.
- `ELA.7.3.1.16` Synthesize visual storytelling techniques to deconstruct a narrative.

#### ELA.7.4 — Misinformation, Clickbait & Fact-Checking

##### ELA.7.4.1 — Fact-Checking and Source Evaluation

- `ELA.7.4.1.1` Identify a lie vs. a truth.
- `ELA.7.4.1.2` Name a person we can trust (parent, teacher).
- `ELA.7.4.1.3` Recall that not everything on a screen is true.
- `ELA.7.4.1.4` Ask 'Who said that?'
- `ELA.7.4.1.5` Summarize why we need to check facts.
- `ELA.7.4.1.6` Explain that anyone can post on the internet.
- `ELA.7.4.1.7` Compare a trustworthy site (.gov, .edu) with a random site.
- `ELA.7.4.1.8` Identify a 'fake news' story (too crazy to be true).
- `ELA.7.4.1.9` Analyze the 'About Us' page of a website.
- `ELA.7.4.1.10` Interpret the difference between Satire (joke) and Hoax.
- `ELA.7.4.1.11` Connect 'Lateral Reading' (opening new tabs to check) to verification.
- `ELA.7.4.1.12` Explain Confirmation Bias (believing what we want to be true).
- `ELA.7.4.1.13` Construct a verification protocol for social media claims.
- `ELA.7.4.1.14` Evaluate the credibility of 'Expert' consensus.
- `ELA.7.4.1.15` Defend the pursuit of objective truth.
- `ELA.7.4.1.16` Synthesize the impact of 'Deepfakes' (AI video) on evidence.

#### ELA.7.5 — Social Media, Algorithms & Echo Chambers

##### ELA.7.5.1 — Digital Citizenship & Online Discourse

- `ELA.7.5.1.1` Identify nice words vs. mean words online.
- `ELA.7.5.1.2` Name the Golden Rule for the internet.
- `ELA.7.5.1.3` Recall that real people are behind the screen.
- `ELA.7.5.1.4` Observe that typing in ALL CAPS looks like shouting.
- `ELA.7.5.1.5` Summarize the rules of 'Netiquette'.
- `ELA.7.5.1.6` Explain why bullying online is dangerous.
- `ELA.7.5.1.7` Compare talking face-to-face with talking online.
- `ELA.7.5.1.8` Apply the rule: 'Think before you post'.
- `ELA.7.5.1.9` Analyze the lack of empathy in digital communication.
- `ELA.7.5.1.10` Interpret the permanence of the Digital Footprint.
- `ELA.7.5.1.11` Connect online behavior to real-world reputation.
- `ELA.7.5.1.12` Explain 'Trolling' and how to handle it (Don't feed the trolls).
- `ELA.7.5.1.13` Construct a personal code of ethics for digital engagement.
- `ELA.7.5.1.14` Evaluate the impact of anonymity on morality.
- `ELA.7.5.1.15` Defend the Christian duty to be peacemakers online.
- `ELA.7.5.1.16` Synthesize James 3 (taming the tongue) with social media usage.

##### ELA.7.5.2 — How Algorithms Curate Feeds

- `ELA.7.5.2.1` Identify that the computer remembers what we watch.
- `ELA.7.5.2.2` Name 'Recommended' videos.
- `ELA.7.5.2.3` Recall that the computer wants us to keep watching.
- `ELA.7.5.2.4` Observe that one video leads to another.
- `ELA.7.5.2.5` Summarize what an algorithm does (sorts information).
- `ELA.7.5.2.6` Explain why you see different things than your friend.
- `ELA.7.5.2.7` Compare a library (you choose) with a feed (it chooses).
- `ELA.7.5.2.8` Identify the 'Rabbit Hole' effect.
- `ELA.7.5.2.9` Analyze how algorithms prioritize engagement (anger/fear).
- `ELA.7.5.2.10` Interpret the 'Filter Bubble' (only seeing what you agree with).
- `ELA.7.5.2.11` Connect data collection to targeted content.
- `ELA.7.5.2.12` Explain the echo chamber effect.
- `ELA.7.5.2.13` Construct a strategy to break out of algorithmic curation.
- `ELA.7.5.2.14` Evaluate the ethical implications of algorithmic radicalization.
- `ELA.7.5.2.15` Defend the need for diverse viewpoints for intellectual growth.
- `ELA.7.5.2.16` Synthesize the relationship between tech business models and social division.

#### ELA.7.6 — Understanding Media Forms & Platforms

##### ELA.7.6.1 — Influencers and Parasocial Relationships

- `ELA.7.6.1.1` Identify a person on a screen who talks to us.
- `ELA.7.6.1.2` Name a favorite YouTuber or character.
- `ELA.7.6.1.3` Recall that they don't actually know us.
- `ELA.7.6.1.4` Observe that they want us to watch more.
- `ELA.7.6.1.5` Summarize what an 'Influencer' does (sells things/ideas).
- `ELA.7.6.1.6` Explain that videos are edited, not real life.
- `ELA.7.6.1.7` Compare a real teacher with an online star.
- `ELA.7.6.1.8` Identify product placements in videos.
- `ELA.7.6.1.9` Analyze the financial incentives behind influencer content.
- `ELA.7.6.1.10` Interpret 'Parasocial Relationships' (one-sided friendship).
- `ELA.7.6.1.11` Connect influencer marketing to consumerism.
- `ELA.7.6.1.12` Explain the difference between authority (expertise) and popularity.
- `ELA.7.6.1.13` Construct a profile of a digital subculture.
- `ELA.7.6.1.14` Evaluate the authenticity of online personas.
- `ELA.7.6.1.15` Defend the biblical warning against the 'fear of man' (approval addiction).
- `ELA.7.6.1.16` Synthesize the shift from institutional trust to personality-based trust.

##### ELA.7.6.2 — Print, Broadcast, and Digital Media

- `ELA.7.6.2.1` Identify different ways we get stories (Books, TV, Tablet).
- `ELA.7.6.2.2` Name a newspaper or magazine.
- `ELA.7.6.2.3` Recall that some things on screens are real and some are made up.
- `ELA.7.6.2.4` Observe that TV shows have commercials.
- `ELA.7.6.2.5` Summarize the difference between News and Entertainment.
- `ELA.7.6.2.6` Explain how a book is different from a website.
- `ELA.7.6.2.7` Compare watching a movie with reading the book.
- `ELA.7.6.2.8` Identify the purpose of a media message (Inform, Persuade, Entertain).
- `ELA.7.6.2.9` Analyze the permanence of print vs. the mutability of digital content.
- `ELA.7.6.2.10` Interpret the credibility of a published book vs. a blog post.

- `ELA.7.6.2.12` Explain the decline of print journalism.

- `ELA.7.6.2.15` Defend the value of deep reading in a skim-reading culture.

##### ELA.7.6.3 — Social Media Ecosystems

- `ELA.7.6.3.1` Identify icons for apps (YouTube, etc.).
- `ELA.7.6.3.2` Name 'sharing' a picture.

- `ELA.7.6.3.8` Identify the difference between a friend and a follower.
- `ELA.7.6.3.9` Analyze the business model of social media (You are the product).
- `ELA.7.6.3.10` Interpret the effect of 'curated lives' on self-esteem.
- `ELA.7.6.3.11` Connect short-form content (TikTok/Reels) to attention span.
- `ELA.7.6.3.12` Explain the concept of 'Virality'.

- `ELA.7.6.3.14` Evaluate the psychological design of gamification in apps.
- `ELA.7.6.3.15` Defend a biblical view of privacy and modesty online.

### ELA.8 — Reading, Phonics & Penmanship (Foundational Literacy)

#### ELA.8.1 — Early Reading Foundations

##### ELA.8.1.1 — Blending and Segmenting

- `ELA.8.1.1.1` Blend sounds to read simple words smoothly.
- `ELA.8.1.1.2` Segment a written word into its individual letters/sounds.
- `ELA.8.1.1.3` Read words with consonant blends (bl, st, tr).
- `ELA.8.1.1.4` Write the sounds heard in a word in the correct order.
- `ELA.8.1.1.5` Blend syllables to read longer compound words.
- `ELA.8.1.1.6` Segment words into roots and affixes.
- `ELA.8.1.1.7` Read words with complex endings (-tion, -ture, -ious).
- `ELA.8.1.1.8` Break down a long word to spell it correctly.
- `ELA.8.1.1.9` Analyze how prefixes change the meaning of a root word.
- `ELA.8.1.1.10` Interpret the structural components of academic terms.
- `ELA.8.1.1.11` Connect segmentation skills to learning foreign vocabulary.
- `ELA.8.1.1.12` Explain the rules for syllable division in English.
- `ELA.8.1.1.13` Construct new words using established blending patterns (neologisms).
- `ELA.8.1.1.14` Evaluate the morphological structure of complex medical or legal terms.
- `ELA.8.1.1.15` Defend the importance of precise articulation in public speaking.
- `ELA.8.1.1.16` Synthesize blending skills to read fluent, expressive prose.

##### ELA.8.1.2 — Decoding Skills

- `ELA.8.1.2.1` Sound out unknown words letter by letter.
- `ELA.8.1.2.2` Use picture clues to help identify a difficult word.
- `ELA.8.1.2.3` Recognize 'chunks' in words (like -ing or -and).
- `ELA.8.1.2.4` Self-correct when a decoded word doesn't make sense.
- `ELA.8.1.2.5` Use context clues to determine the meaning of a decoded word.
- `ELA.8.1.2.6` Decode words with multiple syllables quickly.
- `ELA.8.1.2.7` Identify root words within larger complex words.
- `ELA.8.1.2.8` Apply knowledge of cognates to understand new words.
- `ELA.8.1.2.9` Analyze the structure of a sentence to aid in decoding difficult terms.
- `ELA.8.1.2.10` Interpret words with Greek or Latin roots.
- `ELA.8.1.2.11` Connect decoding fluency to reading comprehension speed.
- `ELA.8.1.2.12` Explain the meaning of a word based on its parts.
- `ELA.8.1.2.13` Construct a glossary of decoded technical terms for a research paper.
- `ELA.8.1.2.14` Evaluate the author's choice of complex vocabulary.
- `ELA.8.1.2.15` Defend an interpretation of a text based on precise word definitions.
- `ELA.8.1.2.16` Synthesize decoding skills to read ancient or primary source documents.

##### ELA.8.1.3 — High-Frequency/Sight Words

- `ELA.8.1.3.1` Recognize the 100 most common words instantly.
- `ELA.8.1.3.2` Read 'rule-breaker' words that can't be sounded out (said, was).
- `ELA.8.1.3.3` Spell common sight words correctly in writing.
- `ELA.8.1.3.4` Read simple sentences fluently without stopping for every word.
- `ELA.8.1.3.5` Recognize the 1,000 most common words instantly.
- `ELA.8.1.3.6` Spell high-frequency words correctly in all written work.
- `ELA.8.1.3.7` Identify homophones (there/their/they're) correctly.
- `ELA.8.1.3.8` Read fluent prose without hesitation on common words.
- `ELA.8.1.3.9` Analyze why certain words became high-frequency in English.
- `ELA.8.1.3.10` Interpret the usage of common academic transition words (however, therefore).
- `ELA.8.1.3.11` Connect sight word fluency to reading stamina.
- `ELA.8.1.3.12` Explain the difference between sight recognition and phonetic decoding.
- `ELA.8.1.3.13` Construct a sophisticated vocabulary beyond high-frequency words.
- `ELA.8.1.3.14` Evaluate the impact of repetitive language in a text.
- `ELA.8.1.3.15` Defend the need for precise vocabulary over common words in academic writing.
- `ELA.8.1.3.16` Synthesize a broad sight vocabulary to read at a collegiate speed.

##### ELA.8.1.4 — Listening to Read-Alouds

- `ELA.8.1.4.1` Sit quietly and listen to a story.
- `ELA.8.1.4.2` Answer simple 'who' and 'what' questions about the story.
- `ELA.8.1.4.3` Predict what might happen next.
- `ELA.8.1.4.4` Identify the feelings of the characters.
- `ELA.8.1.4.5` Summarize the main plot points of a chapter read aloud.
- `ELA.8.1.4.6` Explain the motivation of a character.
- `ELA.8.1.4.7` Compare the read-aloud book with the movie version (if applicable).

##### ELA.8.1.5 — Phonemic Awareness

- `ELA.8.1.5.1` Identify rhyming words in a simple poem or song.
- `ELA.8.1.5.2` Isolate the first sound in a spoken word (e.g., /d/ in dog).
- `ELA.8.1.5.3` Blend spoken sounds together to make a word (/c/-/a/-/t/ -> cat).
- `ELA.8.1.5.4` Segment a spoken word into its individual sounds.
- `ELA.8.1.5.5` Manipulate sounds in words (e.g., change /s/ in 'slip' to /c/ -> 'clip').

- `ELA.8.1.5.7` Distinguish between similar vowel sounds (short e vs. short i).
- `ELA.8.1.5.8` Recognize alliteration and assonance in spoken poetry.
- `ELA.8.1.5.9` Analyze the phonemic structure of complex vocabulary words.
- `ELA.8.1.5.10` Explain how phonemic awareness aids in spelling unfamiliar words.
- `ELA.8.1.5.11` Connect sound patterns to the rhythm and meter of poetry.
- `ELA.8.1.5.12` Identify subtle sound shifts in dialects or accents.

- `ELA.8.1.5.16` Synthesize phonemic knowledge to learn pronunciation in a foreign language.

##### ELA.8.1.6 — Phonics

- `ELA.8.1.6.1` Match letters to their primary sounds (consonants and short vowels).

#### ELA.8.2 — Fluency and Oral Reading

##### ELA.8.2.1 — Accuracy and Rate (WPM)

### ELA.9 — Speech, Rhetoric & Logic (The Trivium's Apex)

#### ELA.9.1 — Classical Rhetoric (Five Canons)

##### ELA.9.1.1 — Arrangement, Style, Memory, Delivery

- `ELA.9.1.1.1` Put story pictures in order (Arrangement).
- `ELA.9.1.1.2` Choose fun words (Style).
- `ELA.9.1.1.3` Remember the story without the book (Memory).
- `ELA.9.1.1.4` Speak with a clear voice (Delivery).
- `ELA.9.1.1.5` Organize points logically (Arrangement).
- `ELA.9.1.1.6` Use strong verbs and adjectives (Style).
- `ELA.9.1.1.7` Use note cards sparingly (Memory).
- `ELA.9.1.1.8` Use hand gestures effectively (Delivery).

- `ELA.9.1.1.11` Connect the structure (Arrangement) to the argument's strength.
- `ELA.9.1.1.12` Explain methods of Loci or Mnemonics for Memory.
- `ELA.9.1.1.13` Construct a speech that balances all five canons.
- `ELA.9.1.1.14` Evaluate the 'High, Middle, and Low' styles of speech.
- `ELA.9.1.1.15` Defend the importance of Memoria for extemporaneous speaking.
- `ELA.9.1.1.16` Synthesize natural talent with disciplined practice in Delivery.

##### ELA.9.1.2 — Invention (Finding Arguments)

- `ELA.9.1.2.1` Think of ideas before speaking.
- `ELA.9.1.2.2` Brainstorm a list of words.
- `ELA.9.1.2.3` Ask 'What do I want to say?'
- `ELA.9.1.2.4` Choose the best idea.
- `ELA.9.1.2.5` Use the '5 Ws' (Who, What, Where, When, Why) to find ideas.
- `ELA.9.1.2.6` Explain the purpose of the speech (inform, persuade, entertain).
- `ELA.9.1.2.7` Brainstorm topics using a mind map.
- `ELA.9.1.2.8` Select the best evidence for a point.
- `ELA.9.1.2.9` Analyze the 'Common Topics' (Definition, Comparison, Relationship, Circumstance).
- `ELA.9.1.2.10` Interpret the audience's needs and values.
- `ELA.9.1.2.11` Connect the topic to a universal theme.
- `ELA.9.1.2.12` Explain the concept of 'Stasis' (the point of disagreement).
- `ELA.9.1.2.13` Construct arguments using the Topoi (places to find arguments).
- `ELA.9.1.2.14` Evaluate the ethos, pathos, and logos of the invention.
- `ELA.9.1.2.15` Defend the necessity of deep research for invention.
- `ELA.9.1.2.16` Synthesize biblical wisdom with rhetorical invention.

#### ELA.9.2 — Debate & Argumentation

##### ELA.9.2.1 — Basic Debate Formats

- `ELA.9.2.1.1` Take turns speaking in a circle.
- `ELA.9.2.1.2` Raise hand to speak.
- `ELA.9.2.1.3` Follow the rules of a class discussion.
- `ELA.9.2.1.4` Vote on a simple class choice.
- `ELA.9.2.1.5` Participate in a structured 'Pro vs. Con' list making.
- `ELA.9.2.1.6` Understand the roles of 'Affirmative' and 'Negative'.
- `ELA.9.2.1.7` Follow a simple time limit for speaking.
- `ELA.9.2.1.8` Judge a debate based on reasons, not popularity.
- `ELA.9.2.1.9` Analyze the structure of a Team Policy debate.
- `ELA.9.2.1.10` Interpret the resolution (the topic being debated).
- `ELA.9.2.1.11` Connect cross-examination questions to setting up an argument.
- `ELA.9.2.1.12` Explain the role of the judge/adjudicator.
- `ELA.9.2.1.13` Construct a case for Lincoln-Douglas (Value) debate.
- `ELA.9.2.1.14` Evaluate the strategic use of time in a debate round.
- `ELA.9.2.1.15` Defend a position you personally disagree with (intellectual exercise).
- `ELA.9.2.1.16` Synthesize flow-charting (taking notes) to track arguments.

##### ELA.9.2.2 — Constructing and Refuting Arguments

- `ELA.9.2.2.1` State an opinion using 'I think...'.
- `ELA.9.2.2.2` Give one reason for the opinion using 'because'.
- `ELA.9.2.2.3` Listen to someone else's opinion without interrupting.
- `ELA.9.2.2.4` Disagree politely ('I think differently').
- `ELA.9.2.2.5` Distinguish between a Fact and an Opinion.
- `ELA.9.2.2.6` Give three reasons to support a claim.
- `ELA.9.2.2.7` Listen to an opposing view and restate it.
- `ELA.9.2.2.8` Respond to a counter-point with 'Yes, but...'.
- `ELA.9.2.2.9` Analyze the 'Burden of Proof' (who has to prove it?).
- `ELA.9.2.2.10` Interpret the opponent's argument to find weaknesses.
- `ELA.9.2.2.11` Connect evidence (stats, quotes) to the claim.
- `ELA.9.2.2.12` Explain the difference between constructive and rebuttal speeches.
- `ELA.9.2.2.13` Construct a formal case with Contentions and Sub-points.
- `ELA.9.2.2.14` Evaluate the validity of the opponent's evidence.
- `ELA.9.2.2.15` Defend a position using the Toulmin Model (Claim, Data, Warrant).
- `ELA.9.2.2.16` Synthesize clash points to summarize the debate.

#### ELA.9.3 — Figures of Speech

##### ELA.9.3.1 — Schemes (Figures of Arrangement)

- `ELA.9.3.1.1` Identify rhyming words.
- `ELA.9.3.1.2` Name words that start with the same sound (Alliteration).
- `ELA.9.3.1.3` Recall repeated words in a song.
- `ELA.9.3.1.4` Observe patterns in sentences.
- `ELA.9.3.1.5` Summarize what a pattern in words is.
- `ELA.9.3.1.6` Explain Parallelism (e.g., 'I came, I saw, I conquered').
- `ELA.9.3.1.7` Compare a normal sentence with a poetic one.
- `ELA.9.3.1.8` Use Anaphora (repeating the start of a sentence).
- `ELA.9.3.1.9` Analyze the effect of Antithesis (contrasting ideas).
- `ELA.9.3.1.10` Interpret the use of Chiasmus (A-B-B-A structure).
- `ELA.9.3.1.11` Connect the scheme to the emphasis of the point.
- `ELA.9.3.1.12` Explain Polysyndeton (many 'ands') vs. Asyndeton (no 'ands').
- `ELA.9.3.1.13` Construct sentences using Tricolon (rule of three).
- `ELA.9.3.1.14` Evaluate the risk of sounding artificial with too many schemes.
- `ELA.9.3.1.15` Defend the use of schemes to aid memory and impact.
- `ELA.9.3.1.16` Synthesize schemes into formal writing and speaking.

##### ELA.9.3.2 — Tropes (Figures of Thought)

- `ELA.9.3.2.1` Identify a simile (Using 'like' or 'as').
- `ELA.9.3.2.2` Name when something is exaggerated.
- `ELA.9.3.2.3` Recall that we don't always mean exactly what we say (e.g., 'I'm freezing').
- `ELA.9.3.2.4` Observe personification (animals talking).
- `ELA.9.3.2.5` Summarize the difference between literal and figurative.
- `ELA.9.3.2.6` Explain a Metaphor.
- `ELA.9.3.2.7` Compare Hyperbole (exaggeration) with Understatement.
- `ELA.9.3.2.8` Identify Irony (saying the opposite of what you mean).
- `ELA.9.3.2.9` Analyze Synecdoche (part for whole) and Metonymy (associated word).
- `ELA.9.3.2.10` Interpret the use of Rhetorical Questions.
- `ELA.9.3.2.11` Connect tropes to the imagination of the listener.
- `ELA.9.3.2.12` Explain the concept of Litotes (negating the contrary).
- `ELA.9.3.2.13` Construct complex metaphors to explain abstract theology.
- `ELA.9.3.2.14` Evaluate the use of Anthimeria (changing part of speech).
- `ELA.9.3.2.15` Defend the use of figurative language in Scripture.
- `ELA.9.3.2.16` Synthesize tropes to create vivid mental images.

#### ELA.9.4 — Formal Logic

##### ELA.9.4.1 — Syllogisms and Deductive Reasoning

- `ELA.9.4.1.1` Sort things into groups (Red things vs. Blue things).
- `ELA.9.4.1.2` Identify patterns (A, B, A, B...).
- `ELA.9.4.1.3` Recall that if all dogs bark, and Fido is a dog, Fido barks.
- `ELA.9.4.1.4` Observe that some things must be true if other things are true.
- `ELA.9.4.1.5` Summarize an 'If... Then...' statement.
- `ELA.9.4.1.6` Explain what a premise is (a starting fact).
- `ELA.9.4.1.7` Compare General rules to Specific examples.
- `ELA.9.4.1.8` Identify a logical conclusion.
- `ELA.9.4.1.9` Analyze the structure of a Categorical Syllogism (All A are B...).
- `ELA.9.4.1.10` Interpret the difference between Valid (structure) and Sound (truth).
- `ELA.9.4.1.11` Connect logic to the nature of God (Logos).
- `ELA.9.4.1.12` Explain Deductive vs. Inductive reasoning.
- `ELA.9.4.1.13` Construct valid syllogisms (Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens).
- `ELA.9.4.1.14` Evaluate the 'Undistributed Middle' term error.
- `ELA.9.4.1.15` Defend the laws of logic (Identity, Non-Contradiction, Excluded Middle).
- `ELA.9.4.1.16` Synthesize formal logic with propositional logic (basic symbols).

#### ELA.9.5 — Informal Logic & Fallacies

##### ELA.9.5.1 — Common Fallacies

- `ELA.9.5.1.1` Identify when an answer doesn't fit the question.
- `ELA.9.5.1.2` Name 'name-calling' as a bad way to argue.
- `ELA.9.5.1.3` Recall that just because a friend does it, doesn't mean it's right.
- `ELA.9.5.1.4` Observe that two wrongs don't make a right.
- `ELA.9.5.1.5` Summarize the Ad Hominem fallacy (attacking the person).
- `ELA.9.5.1.6` Explain the Bandwagon fallacy (everyone is doing it).
- `ELA.9.5.1.7` Compare a good reason with a bad excuse.
- `ELA.9.5.1.8` Identify a Straw Man (pretending the other side is silly).
- `ELA.9.5.1.9` Analyze the Red Herring (distraction).
- `ELA.9.5.1.10` Interpret the Circular Reasoning fallacy (begging the question).
- `ELA.9.5.1.11` Connect the Post Hoc fallacy to superstition (it happened after, so it was caused by).
- `ELA.9.5.1.12` Explain the Slippery Slope argument.
- `ELA.9.5.1.13` Construct a critique of a political ad detecting fallacies.
- `ELA.9.5.1.14` Evaluate the Tu Quoque ('you too') defense.
- `ELA.9.5.1.15` Defend truth without resorting to fallacious reasoning.
- `ELA.9.5.1.16` Synthesize the study of fallacies to sharpen critical listening.

#### ELA.9.6 — Oral Interpretation & Recitation

##### ELA.9.6.1 — Dramatic Scripture Reading

- `ELA.9.6.1.1` Read a Bible verse clearly.
- `ELA.9.6.1.2` Hold the Bible respectfully while reading.
- `ELA.9.6.1.3` Say the book, chapter, and verse numbers.
- `ELA.9.6.1.4` Listen quietly while others read the Bible.
- `ELA.9.6.1.5` Read a narrative passage (e.g., David and Goliath) with expression.
- `ELA.9.6.1.6` Project voice so the back of the room can hear.
- `ELA.9.6.1.7` Pronounce biblical names correctly.
- `ELA.9.6.1.8` Apply a reverent tone to the reading of God's Word.
- `ELA.9.6.1.9` Analyze the genre of the passage to determine reading style.
- `ELA.9.6.1.10` Interpret the emotional context of a Psalm or Lament.
- `ELA.9.6.1.11` Connect the reading to the listeners' understanding.
- `ELA.9.6.1.12` Explain the concept of 'Lector'.
- `ELA.9.6.1.13` Construct a prepared reading for a church service.
- `ELA.9.6.1.14` Evaluate the pacing required for a congregation to follow.
- `ELA.9.6.1.15` Defend the public reading of Scripture as a central act of worship (1 Tim 4:13).
- `ELA.9.6.1.16` Synthesize vocal variety to highlight theological emphasis.

##### ELA.9.6.2 — Reading Poetry Aloud

- `ELA.9.6.2.1` Recite a nursery rhyme from memory.
- `ELA.9.6.2.2` Use a happy or sad voice to match the poem.
- `ELA.9.6.2.3` Say rhyming words clearly.
- `ELA.9.6.2.4` Stand still while reciting.
- `ELA.9.6.2.5` Read a poem paying attention to punctuation (not just line breaks).
- `ELA.9.6.2.6` Use volume changes to make the poem interesting.
- `ELA.9.6.2.7` Memorize a classic poem (e.g., Stevenson or Rossetti).
- `ELA.9.6.2.8` Identify the rhythm while reading.
- `ELA.9.6.2.9` Analyze the meter (iambic, etc.) to guide pronunciation.
- `ELA.9.6.2.10` Interpret the mood of the poem through tone and pacing.
- `ELA.9.6.2.11` Connect the sound devices (alliteration) to the delivery.
- `ELA.9.6.2.12` Explain the difference between 'acting' and 'interpreting'.
- `ELA.9.6.2.13` Construct a performance of a complex poem (e.g., Eliot or Donne).
- `ELA.9.6.2.14` Evaluate the prosody of a recorded performance.
- `ELA.9.6.2.15` Defend interpretation choices based on the text.
- `ELA.9.6.2.16` Synthesize facial expression and vocal modulation.

#### ELA.9.7 — Public Speaking & Presentation

##### ELA.9.7.1 — Organizing a Speech

- `ELA.9.7.1.1` Tell a story with a beginning, middle, and end.
- `ELA.9.7.1.2` Stick to one main idea when talking.
- `ELA.9.7.1.3` Start with a 'Hello' and end with 'Thank you'.
- `ELA.9.7.1.4` Use pictures to help remember what to say.
- `ELA.9.7.1.5` Structure a speech with an Introduction, Body, and Conclusion.
- `ELA.9.7.1.6` Use 'signpost' words (First, Next, Finally).
- `ELA.9.7.1.7` Create a strong opening hook (question, fact, story).
- `ELA.9.7.1.8` Summarize the main points at the end.
- `ELA.9.7.1.9` Analyze the logical flow of a famous speech.
- `ELA.9.7.1.10` Interpret the 'Exordium' (Introduction) and 'Peroration' (Conclusion).
- `ELA.9.7.1.11` Connect the main points to a central thesis statement.
- `ELA.9.7.1.12` Explain the importance of transitions between arguments.
- `ELA.9.7.1.13` Construct a complex speech using classical arrangement (Dispositio).
- `ELA.9.7.1.14` Evaluate the effectiveness of different organizational patterns (chronological vs. topical).
- `ELA.9.7.1.15` Defend the necessity of a clear 'call to action'.
- `ELA.9.7.1.16` Synthesize evidence and narrative into a cohesive argument.

##### ELA.9.7.2 — Overcoming Stage Fright

- `ELA.9.7.2.1` Stand up straight and look at the audience.
- `ELA.9.7.2.2` Speak loudly enough to be heard by everyone.
- `ELA.9.7.2.3` Share a 'Show and Tell' item with confidence.
- `ELA.9.7.2.4` Identify that butterflies in the stomach are normal.
- `ELA.9.7.2.5` Use deep breathing to calm nerves before speaking.
- `ELA.9.7.2.6` Practice a speech in front of a mirror or family.
- `ELA.9.7.2.7` Maintain eye contact with different parts of the room.
- `ELA.9.7.2.8` Turn nervous energy into enthusiasm.
- `ELA.9.7.2.9` Analyze the physical symptoms of anxiety vs. excitement.
- `ELA.9.7.2.10` Interpret the audience's body language to gain confidence.
- `ELA.9.7.2.11` Connect preparation and practice to reduced anxiety.
- `ELA.9.7.2.12` Explain the concept of 'posture' and 'presence'.
- `ELA.9.7.2.13` Construct a personal routine for pre-speech preparation.
- `ELA.9.7.2.14` Evaluate the psychology of public speaking anxiety.
- `ELA.9.7.2.15` Defend the message even when feeling fear.
- `ELA.9.7.2.16` Synthesize vulnerability and authority in delivery.

##### ELA.9.7.3 — Visual Aids and Presentation Tools

- `ELA.9.7.3.1` Hold an object so everyone can see it.
- `ELA.9.7.3.2` Draw a picture to show the class.
- `ELA.9.7.3.3` Point to parts of a picture while talking.
- `ELA.9.7.3.4` Use a prop to tell a story.
- `ELA.9.7.3.5` Create a poster with clear text and images.
- `ELA.9.7.3.6` Use a digital slide to show a photo.
- `ELA.9.7.3.7` Explain a diagram or map to an audience.
- `ELA.9.7.3.8` Avoid reading directly off the poster.
- `ELA.9.7.3.9` Analyze the 'less is more' rule for slide text.
- `ELA.9.7.3.10` Interpret the impact of color and font choice on readability.
- `ELA.9.7.3.11` Connect the visual aid to the spoken point (don't distract).
- `ELA.9.7.3.12` Explain how to cite sources on a slide.
- `ELA.9.7.3.13` Construct a professional slide deck (e.g., PowerPoint/Keynote).
- `ELA.9.7.3.14` Evaluate the rhetorical impact of data visualization.
- `ELA.9.7.3.15` Defend the choice of analog vs. digital aids for specific contexts.
- `ELA.9.7.3.16` Synthesize speech and visuals for a seamless presentation.

#### ELA.9.8 — Socratic Dialogue & Discussion

##### ELA.9.8.1 — Asking Good Questions

- `ELA.9.8.1.1` Ask 'Why?' to understand better.
- `ELA.9.8.1.2` Listen to the answer before talking again.
- `ELA.9.8.1.3` Take turns in a circle discussion.
- `ELA.9.8.1.4` Ask politely for information.
- `ELA.9.8.1.5` Ask open-ended questions (not just Yes/No).
- `ELA.9.8.1.6` Explain what someone else said to check understanding.
- `ELA.9.8.1.7` Compare two different answers to the same question.
- `ELA.9.8.1.8` Ask 'What do you mean by that?'
- `ELA.9.8.1.9` Analyze assumptions behind a statement.
- `ELA.9.8.1.10` Interpret the Socratic method (teaching by asking).
- `ELA.9.8.1.11` Connect questions to discovering truth together.
- `ELA.9.8.1.12` Explain the value of admitting 'I don't know'.
- `ELA.9.8.1.13` Construct a line of questioning to expose a contradiction.
- `ELA.9.8.1.14` Evaluate the definition of terms in a discussion.
- `ELA.9.8.1.15` Defend the pursuit of Truth over the pursuit of winning.
- `ELA.9.8.1.16` Synthesize the dialectic process (Thesis-Antithesis-Synthesis).

### ELA.10 — Spelling, Vocabulary & Word Study

#### ELA.10.1 — Greek and Latin Roots and Affixes

##### ELA.10.1.1 — Common Greek and Latin Roots

- `ELA.10.1.1.1` Identify word parts that look the same (e.g., play in playing/played).
- `ELA.10.1.1.2` Name simple prefixes like 'un-' (not).
- `ELA.10.1.1.3` Recall that big words are made of small parts.
- `ELA.10.1.1.4` Observe that 'bi-' means two (bicycle).
- `ELA.10.1.1.5` Summarize the meaning of common roots (struct, port, graph).
- `ELA.10.1.1.6` Explain how 'tele' means far (telephone, television).
- `ELA.10.1.1.7` Categorize words by their root family.
- `ELA.10.1.1.8` Apply root knowledge to guess the meaning of a new word.
- `ELA.10.1.1.9` Analyze how 'spect' (to look) appears in inspect, spectacle, spectator.
- `ELA.10.1.1.10` Interpret the difference between Greek roots (often scientific) and Latin roots.
- `ELA.10.1.1.11` Connect 'chron' to time and 'geo' to earth.
- `ELA.10.1.1.12` Explain how roots build academic vocabulary.
- `ELA.10.1.1.13` Construct a breakdown of complex words like 'antidisestablishmentarianism'.
- `ELA.10.1.1.14` Evaluate the nuance added by specific roots.
- `ELA.10.1.1.15` Perform research on the etymology of a specific root.
- `ELA.10.1.1.16` Synthesize root knowledge to decipher medical or legal terminology.

##### ELA.10.1.2 — Prefixes and Suffixes

- `ELA.10.1.2.1` Identify 're-' means to do again.
- `ELA.10.1.2.2` Name '-er' as a person who does something (teacher, painter).
- `ELA.10.1.2.3` Recall that '-s' means more than one.
- `ELA.10.1.2.4` Add endings to simple words.
- `ELA.10.1.2.5` Summarize how prefixes change the meaning of a word.
- `ELA.10.1.2.6` Explain how suffixes change the part of speech (quick -> quickly).
- `ELA.10.1.2.7` Compare 'un-' and 'dis-' (both mean not/opposite).
- `ELA.10.1.2.8` Use '-ful' and '-less' correctly.
- `ELA.10.1.2.9` Analyze the function of prefixes like 'anti-', 'inter-', 'trans-'.
- `ELA.10.1.2.10` Interpret abstract suffixes like '-ism', '-ology', '-tion'.
- `ELA.10.1.2.11` Connect affixes to the modification of root meanings.
- `ELA.10.1.2.12` Explain how '-able' and '-ible' differ.
- `ELA.10.1.2.13` Construct new words using standard affixes (neologisms).
- `ELA.10.1.2.14` Evaluate the precise meaning of words like 'amoral' vs. 'immoral'.
- `ELA.10.1.2.15` Defend word choices based on the specific shade of meaning provided by an affix.
- `ELA.10.1.2.16` Synthesize morphological analysis for reading comprehension.

#### ELA.10.2 — Orthography and Patterns

##### ELA.10.2.1 — Homophones and Homographs

- `ELA.10.2.1.1` Identify words that sound the same but mean different things.
- `ELA.10.2.1.2` Name pairs like 'see' and 'sea'.
- `ELA.10.2.1.3` Recall which 'two/to/too' to use in a simple sentence.
- `ELA.10.2.1.4` Observe that spelling changes the meaning.
- `ELA.10.2.1.5` Summarize the definitions of homophones, homographs, and homonyms.
- `ELA.10.2.1.6` Explain the difference between 'their', 'there', and 'they're'.
- `ELA.10.2.1.7` Compare 'its' and 'it's'.
- `ELA.10.2.1.8` Use the correct homophone in writing.
- `ELA.10.2.1.9` Analyze context clues to determine the meaning of a homograph.
- `ELA.10.2.1.10` Interpret the correct usage of 'affect' vs. 'effect'.
- `ELA.10.2.1.11` Connect spelling to meaning in homophones.
- `ELA.10.2.1.12` Explain why homophones cause confusion.
- `ELA.10.2.1.13` Construct sentences using challenging homophones correctly (e.g., principal/principle).
- `ELA.10.2.1.14` Evaluate the clarity of writing based on word choice.
- `ELA.10.2.1.15` Defend the importance of distinguishing between similar words.
- `ELA.10.2.1.16` Synthesize an understanding of nuance in word usage.

##### ELA.10.2.2 — Silent Letters and Oddities

- `ELA.10.2.2.1` Identify the 'magic e' that makes no sound.
- `ELA.10.2.2.2` Name words with silent letters like 'knee' or 'lamb'.
- `ELA.10.2.2.3` Recall that we don't say every letter we see.
- `ELA.10.2.2.4` Copy words with tricky spellings.
- `ELA.10.2.2.5` Summarize patterns of silent letters (kn-, wr-, -mb).
- `ELA.10.2.2.6` Explain that some English words come from other languages.
- `ELA.10.2.2.7` Categorize words with silent 'gh' (e.g., high, thought).
- `ELA.10.2.2.8` Apply memory tricks to spell 'weird' words.
- `ELA.10.2.2.9` Analyze why certain letters became silent over time (historical linguistics).
- `ELA.10.2.2.10` Interpret the spelling of 'muscle' vs. 'muscular' (the silent c).
- `ELA.10.2.2.11` Connect silent letters to word origins.
- `ELA.10.2.2.12` Explain the 'Great Vowel Shift' in simple terms.
- `ELA.10.2.2.13` Construct an explanation for the spelling of 'colonel' or 'bologna'.
- `ELA.10.2.2.14` Evaluate the irregularities of English orthography.
- `ELA.10.2.2.15` Defend the preservation of etymological spelling.
- `ELA.10.2.2.16` Synthesize knowledge of oddities to master spelling bees or advanced writing.

#### ELA.10.3 — Spelling Foundations and Rules

##### ELA.10.3.1 — Common Spelling Rules

- `ELA.10.3.1.1` Identify that 'q' is almost always followed by 'u'.
- `ELA.10.3.1.2` Name the rule: 'i before e except after c'.
- `ELA.10.3.1.3` Recall that sentences start with a capital letter.
- `ELA.10.3.1.4` Observe that names start with a capital letter.
- `ELA.10.3.1.5` Summarize rules for making plurals (-s, -es, -ies).
- `ELA.10.3.1.6` Explain when to drop the 'e' before adding a suffix.
- `ELA.10.3.1.7` Apply the rule for changing 'y' to 'i'.
- `ELA.10.3.1.8` Compare singular and plural spelling patterns.
- `ELA.10.3.1.9` Analyze the exceptions to the 'i before e' rule.
- `ELA.10.3.1.10` Interpret rules for adding suffixes to words ending in consonants.

#### ELA.11.8 — The Writing Process and Writer’s Habits

##### ELA.11.8.1 — Drafting

- `ELA.11.8.1.1` Write sentences to tell a story.
- `ELA.11.8.1.2` Use 'best guess' spelling to keep writing moving.
- `ELA.11.8.1.3` Write from left to right and top to bottom.

- `ELA.11.8.1.8` Focus on content rather than perfect mechanics during the first draft.

- `ELA.11.8.1.10` Integrate quotes or evidence into the draft.
- `ELA.11.8.1.11` Maintain a consistent voice and tone.
- `ELA.11.8.1.12` Experiment with sentence variety during drafting.
- `ELA.11.8.1.13` Construct a cohesive argument that sustains a thesis throughout.
- `ELA.11.8.1.14` Evaluate the flow of logic while drafting.
- `ELA.11.8.1.15` Draft with specific rhetorical strategies in mind.
- `ELA.11.8.1.16` Produce a substantial draft ready for rigorous critique.

##### ELA.11.8.2 — Editing

- `ELA.11.8.2.1` Circle misspelled words.
- `ELA.11.8.2.2` Check for capital letters at the start of sentences.
- `ELA.11.8.2.3` Check for periods at the end of sentences.
- `ELA.11.8.2.4` Make sure handwriting is readable.

- `ELA.11.8.2.9` Analyze sentence structure for variety and flow.
- `ELA.11.8.2.10` Correct comma splices and misplaced modifiers.
- `ELA.11.8.2.11` Ensure consistent verb tense throughout.
- `ELA.11.8.2.12` Format citations correctly.
- `ELA.11.8.2.13` Perform a rigorous copy-edit for standard English conventions.
- `ELA.11.8.2.14` Evaluate the use of advanced punctuation (semicolons, colons).
- `ELA.11.8.2.15` Defend stylistic choices against standard grammar rules when intentional.
- `ELA.11.8.2.16` Produce a polished manuscript free of mechanical errors.

##### ELA.11.8.3 — Prewriting

- `ELA.11.8.3.1` Draw a picture to plan what to write.
- `ELA.11.8.3.2` Talk about ideas with a teacher before writing.
- `ELA.11.8.3.3` Make a simple list of words to use.

- `ELA.11.8.3.9` Construct a detailed alphanumeric outline.
- `ELA.11.8.3.10` Research background information to inform the plan.
- `ELA.11.8.3.11` Analyze the prompt to ensure the purpose is met.
- `ELA.11.8.3.12` Use free-writing techniques to overcome writer's block.
- `ELA.11.8.3.13` Evaluate the effectiveness of different prewriting strategies for different tasks.
- `ELA.11.8.3.14` Develop a thesis statement that guides the entire structure.
- `ELA.11.8.3.15` Defend the organization of the argument prior to drafting.
- `ELA.11.8.3.16` Synthesize research notes into a coherent plan.

##### ELA.11.8.4 — Revising

- `ELA.11.8.4.1` Add a detail to a drawing or sentence.
- `ELA.11.8.4.2` Change a boring word to an interesting word.
- `ELA.11.8.4.3` Read the writing aloud to see if it makes sense.
- `ELA.11.8.4.4` Add a missing period or capital letter.

- `ELA.11.8.4.6` Move sentences to make the order better.
- `ELA.11.8.4.7` Remove repetitive words or sentences.
- `ELA.11.8.4.8` Check if the writing stays on topic.
- `ELA.11.8.4.9` Analyze the strength of the thesis statement.
- `ELA.11.8.4.10` Improve transitions between paragraphs.
- `ELA.11.8.4.11` Replace passive voice with active voice where appropriate.
- `ELA.11.8.4.12` Show, don't tell (replace summary with description).
- `ELA.11.8.4.13` Evaluate the rhetorical effectiveness of the piece.
- `ELA.11.8.4.14` Reorganize entire sections to improve logical progression.
- `ELA.11.8.4.15` Critique the clarity and precision of the language.
- `ELA.11.8.4.16` Synthesize feedback from peers or mentors to rewrite substantive portions.

## GEO — Geography

### GEO.1 — Geographical Skills, Fieldwork & Geospatial Technology

#### GEO.1.1 — Advanced Cartography & GIS

##### GEO.1.1.1 — Map Projections and Distortions

- `GEO.1.1.1.1` Identify a globe as the only true map.

- `GEO.1.1.1.3` Recall that peeling an orange flat tears the skin.
- `GEO.1.1.1.4` Observe how Greenland looks huge on some maps.

- `GEO.1.1.1.6` Explain the trade-off between size and shape accuracy.
- `GEO.1.1.1.7` Compare the Robinson projection with the Gall-Peters.

- `GEO.1.1.1.9` Analyze the political implications of map distortion (Eurocentrism).
- `GEO.1.1.1.10` Interpret the Tissot's Indicatrix (circles showing distortion).
- `GEO.1.1.1.11` Connect the purpose of the map to the choice of projection (navigation vs. area).
- `GEO.1.1.1.12` Explain Conic, Cylindrical, and Azimuthal projections.
- `GEO.1.1.1.13` Construct a comparison of the Winkel Tripel and Mercator.
- `GEO.1.1.1.14` Evaluate the use of the Polar projection for air travel.
- `GEO.1.1.1.15` Defend the mathematical necessity of distortion when flattening a sphere.
- `GEO.1.1.1.16` Synthesize geometry with cartographic history.

## SCI — Science & Nature

### SCI.1 — Applied Science, Technology & Engineering (STEM)

#### SCI.1.1 — Engineering & Design (Practical Application of Physics)

- `SCI.1.1.1.1` Identify basic parts on a simple picture plan (door, window, wheel).

- `SCI.1.1.1.9` Interpret multi-view orthographic projections and scale drawings.

- `SCI.1.1.1.12` Critique poorly drawn plans and revise for clarity.

##### SCI.1.1.2 — Bridge & Structure Building (Truss Systems, Arches)

##### SCI.1.1.3 — Engineering Design Cycle (ask, imagine, plan, create, improve, present)

- `SCI.1.1.3.1` Identify a simple problem in daily life and suggest a way to fix it with available materials.

- `SCI.1.1.3.6` Sketch a labeled plan before building.

- `SCI.1.1.3.8` Test a model, record what happened, and suggest one improvement.
- `SCI.1.1.3.9` Analyze a real-world problem and develop criteria and constraints for a solution.

- `SCI.1.1.3.16` Synthesize biblical wisdom literature (Prov 8; 24:3–4) with modern engineering principles.
